releases.notes:
**MAJOR UPDATE — Werewolf brothers join the pack, and Howling Werewolf comes to Fabric!** Summon a wandering werewolf merchant, recruit him as a lasting companion, and send your pack to guard, hunt and even tidy your storage. This release also adds **Minecraft 1.21.11 on Fabric**, and redesigns the werewolf progression screen and the companion UI with a smoother look.

This is the first public release since 1.2.2, so the notes below cover everything added since then.

## 1. Werewolf brothers: merchants and companions
The Moon-Oath altars now answer a second rite. Learn **Pack Oath** on the skill tree, build the altars the same way as for the Alpha Trial, place a **Wolfsbane** on each outer altar and a **Moonbane Pearl** in the centre, then right-click the central altar with an empty hand. A werewolf brother runs in from afar and stays for 10 minutes, at any time of day and any moon phase.
- **Trade:** each merchant brings 6 of 9 trades for Silver Ingots, Wolfsbane, Moonbane Pearls, Werewolf Potions and Wolfsbane Potions. Uses are limited and do not restock.
- **Recruit:** right-click him while holding an **Alpha Werewolf Badge** and confirm. You can keep one companion before the Alpha Trial, and up to three after it, one per Pack Oath rank.
- **Orders:** Follow, Guard, Rest, Sort and Hunt.
  - Only Guard fights: it joins your attacks, protects you and strikes back.
  - Monsters leave a following, resting or sorting companion alone.
- **Sort:** the companion walks around and tidies chests, barrels and, on 1.21.11 and 26.1.2, copper chests, within 16 blocks.
  - Hang a filled item frame on a container to choose what it keeps.
  - Containers it cannot walk up to are sorted from up to 32 blocks away.
- **Hunt:** it leaves for 1.5–3 Minecraft days and brings back meat, hides, ores and more, then rests for two days.
- **Grow:** raise a companion from tier 0 to tier 3 with Moonbane Pearls (2 / 4 / 8). Each tier adds health, damage, damage reduction and regeneration.
- **Care:** recall it from any dimension, revive it with a badge, rename it, change its coat, open its nine-slot pack, or dismiss it (its pack is handed back to you).
- Press **C** for the companion window. The window has a built-in guide, and companions address you as **"my Alpha"** by default; you can change this.

Full guide: [Companions](https://github.com/R-Eatch/howling-werewolf/blob/main/docs/COMPANIONS.md) · [Hunt and trade tables](https://github.com/R-Eatch/howling-werewolf/blob/main/docs/COMPANION-TABLES.md)

## 2. Now on Fabric
Howling Werewolf is now available for **Minecraft 1.21.11 on Fabric**, with the same content as the other editions. It requires **Fabric API**.

## 3. A new progression screen
- The **K** screen has been redrawn as a moonlit canvas. It shows tonight's real moon phase, your form standing before the moon, and your skills along its arcs.
- Use the crescent in the top-right corner to switch between the white **Moonlight** and dark **Nightfall** themes.
- **Long Claws, Tool Claws and Fire Claws** can now be switched off and on again on the Abilities page. Switching costs and refunds nothing.
- The **Equipment: shown / hidden** choice on the skin page is now applied and saved with your skin, and other players see it too.
- If you are not a werewolf yet, the K screen now tells you how to become one.

## 4. Animation, rendering and compatibility
- **Modern Beast:**
  - Its forelimbs now step in pairs.
  - Sprinting turns into a four-legged run, and crouching into a low four-legged prowl.
- **First-person arm fur** now shows on 1.20.1, 1.21.1 and 1.21.11, matching 26.1.2.
- **Sodium and Xenon:** Modern textures no longer shift out of place.
- **Iron's Spells and Better Combat:** when they draw your body in first person, the werewolf model no longer blocks the camera. Third person is unchanged.
- The merchant now uses wolf sounds instead of villager sounds while trading.

## 5. Configuration, commands and new guides

releases.notes:
**MAJOR UPDATE — Meet the new Modern models!** This release brings a fresh look to all three werewolf forms, with **27 new textures**, updated animations, and improved equipment rendering.

## 1. Modern models and textures
The new **Modern** model set covers all three forms: **Werewolf, Quadruped Wolf, and Beast**. Each form comes with **nine texture variants**, bringing the total to **27**, with animations adapted to the new models.
A huge thank-you to **thewolfulti** for creating and sharing these models and textures! The contributed assets are licensed under **CC BY-SA 4.0**, consistent with the mod's existing art license.

## 2. Switching models and configuring NPCs
**Modern is the default for new players.** If you're using an existing save, open the werewolf menu, go to **Skins**, and use the button in the **top-right corner** to switch between **Modern** and **Classic**. Classic is the original model set and remains fully available.
To choose which models werewolf NPCs use, open `config/howlingwerewolf-common.toml` and set the following option under `[gameplay]`:
```toml
npcModelSet = "modern"
```
Use `"modern"` for wild werewolves, the Alpha, and its summoned pack to use the new models and textures, or `"classic"` to keep their original appearance.

## 3. Animation and equipment rendering
This update adapts animations to the new models and fixes several animation and held-item rendering issues. **Elytra also have dedicated rendering support and now display correctly.**
Some equipment may still appear incorrectly on Modern models. If you prefer the original equipment appearance, switch to **Classic** or **disable equipment rendering** in the config.

---

Enjoy the new looks, and have fun!

releases.notes:
Since version 1.0.7, Howling Werewolf has received a major update: three new skins have been added, bringing the total to four switchable in-game skins including the original Adrian coat, along with support for importing custom skins.

* Four built-in skins are now available across Werewolf, Quadruped Wolf, and Beast forms: Adrian, Ashen, Onyx, and Ivory.
* Added an interactive skin preview with form selection, rotation, zoom, mouse tracking, and an equipment visibility toggle.
* Added a Skins menu, paged skin browsing, and a Resource Packs shortcut.
* Added custom skin support through resource packs, including in-game template export, Blockbench painting templates, and English and Chinese creation guides.
* Added multiplayer skin synchronization. Custom skins require the same resource pack on each client; if a skin is missing, Adrian is shown as a temporary fallback without overwriting the saved selection.
* Adjusted the Skill Tree layout by moving Level Reset below the skill list.

Version 1.1.2 has passed in-game testing.

For multiplayer, both the server and clients should be updated to 1.1.2, as the new skin synchronization protocol is not compatible with earlier versions.
